quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #10
										  					
  

25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: Which statement is true about large trucks?

options.text: They take longer to stop than passenger vehicles.
They all have air brakes that let them stop quickly.
They are easier to steer than passenger vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: They take longer to stop than passenger vehicles.
questions.explanation: Large trucks need more distance to stop than other vehicles going the same speed. A passenger car going 55 mph stops in about 400 feet. A large truck at the same speed needs almost 800 feet to stop.

questions.question: Which habit is dangerous in work zones?

options.text: Following another vehicle too closely
Not watching carefully for workers and equipment
Both of the above

questions.correctAnswerText: Both of the above
questions.explanation: In a work zone, slow down for traffic and keep a safe distance from other vehicles. Watch closely for workers and machinery in the area.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Reserved parking for people with disabilities.
Slow-moving vehicle.
No U-turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Reserved parking for people with disabilities.
questions.explanation: This sign shows parking spaces reserved for vehicles with disabled parking permits, Persons with Disabilities license plates, or Disabled Veteran license plates.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Winding road
Loose gravel
Slippery when wet

questions.correctAnswerText: Slippery when wet
questions.explanation: This sign warns that the road may be slippery when it rains. Drive carefully on slippery roads.

questions.question: You are on the freeway behind a large truck. You should drive:

options.text: Close behind the truck in bad weather because the driver can see farther than you.
Farther behind the truck than you would a passenger vehicle.
One car length behind the truck so the driver can see you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Farther behind the truck than you would a passenger vehicle.
questions.explanation: If you follow too close behind a truck, the driver cannot see you in their mirrors. Tailgating is dangerous because you lose your safety cushion if the truck stops suddenly.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Four lanes of traffic ahead.
Divided highway ahead.
Two-way traffic ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Two-way traffic ahead.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black words. They tell you about conditions coming up. This sign warns that you are leaving a one-way highway and entering a two-way highway.

questions.question: When driving near a large commercial vehicle, you should:

options.text: Follow close to reduce wind drag on your vehicle.
Avoid driving beside it for long periods.
Drive on its right side when going around curves and hills.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid driving beside it for long periods.
questions.explanation: Large commercial vehicles have big blind spots on both sides. Do not drive beside them for long periods because the driver may not see you.

questions.question: When changing lanes, check your blind spot by:

options.text: Using the rearview mirror.
Turning your head and looking over your shoulder.
Using your side mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turning your head and looking over your shoulder.
questions.explanation: Even with mirrors, there are blind spots you cannot see. Before changing lanes, look over your shoulder to check these hidden areas.

questions.question: When pulling into traffic from a parked spot, you should:

options.text: Drive slower than other traffic for 200 feet.
Wait for a large gap so you can match the speed of traffic.
Wait for the first two vehicles to pass, then enter the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait for a large gap so you can match the speed of traffic.
questions.explanation: When merging into traffic, wait for a gap large enough for your vehicle to reach the same speed as other cars.

questions.question: Which action blocks the smooth flow of traffic?

options.text: Slowing down to look at a crash.
Avoiding unnecessary lane changes.
Using public transportation instead of your own vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slowing down to look at a crash.
questions.explanation: Slowing down to look at crashes causes traffic jams and should be avoided.

questions.question: As you drive faster, what is important to do?

options.text: Turn on your headlights.
Look far ahead of your vehicle.
Change lanes often.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look far ahead of your vehicle.
questions.explanation: Your vehicle needs more distance to stop as you go faster. When driving at high speeds, look far ahead so you have time to safely react to dangers.

questions.question: When passing another car, when is it safe to return to your lane?

options.text: When the other driver signals for you to move back.
When you look over your shoulder and see the car behind you.
When you can see both headlights of the other car in your rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you can see both headlights of the other car in your rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: Before you return to your lane after passing, make sure there is a safe gap between you and the other car. When both headlights appear in your rearview mirror, it is safe to return to your lane.

questions.question: At a railroad crossing, you must:

options.text: Watch for vehicles that must stop at railroad crossings, like school buses and trucks with hazardous materials.
Watch for trains coming from either direction.
Do both A and B.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do both A and B.
questions.explanation: Approach all railroad crossings with great caution. Only cross when you are sure no train is coming from either direction. Also watch for vehicles that must stop at railroad crossings, such as school buses and trucks carrying hazardous materials.

questions.question: Any amount of alcohol in your blood may affect:

options.text: Your right-of-way privileges.
Your judgment and physical coordination.
Your knowledge.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your judgment and physical coordination.
questions.explanation: Even a small amount of alcohol can make it unsafe to drive. Any alcohol can affect your judgment and ability to move your body properly. Driving with any amount of alcohol can result in criminal charges.

questions.question: What does a red arrow pointing right on a traffic light mean?

options.text: You may turn right after slowing down and checking for traffic.
You cannot turn right until the light turns green.
You may turn right after coming to a complete stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: You cannot turn right until the light turns green.
questions.explanation: A red arrow means stop. You must stay stopped until a green light or green arrow appears. Never turn against a red arrow.

questions.question: Backing up your vehicle is:

options.text: Always dangerous.
Dangerous only if you have a helper.
Dangerous only in large vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always dangerous.
questions.explanation: Backing up is always dangerous because you cannot see well behind your vehicle. Use extra care when backing up.

questions.question: Which statement is true about driving and taking medicine?

options.text: Most cold medicines can make you drowsy.
Over-the-counter medicines cannot affect your driving if you take the recommended dose.
Any medicine prescribed by a doctor is safe to take while driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Most cold medicines can make you drowsy.
questions.explanation: All medicines, whether prescription or over-the-counter, can be dangerous and may affect your driving. Cold and allergy medicines can make you drowsy and reduce your driving ability. You must know how your medicine affects your ability to drive safely.

questions.question: With a Class C driver license, you may drive:

options.text: Any motor vehicle, no matter its size or weight.
A vehicle weighing less than 26,001 pounds.
A vehicle weighing more than 26,001 pounds.

questions.correctAnswerText: A vehicle weighing less than 26,001 pounds.
questions.explanation: With a Class C license, you may drive any vehicle that weighs less than 26,001 pounds.

questions.question: When driving at night, you should:

options.text: Always use your high beams.
Look directly at the headlights of oncoming vehicles.
Stay farther behind other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay farther behind other vehicles.
questions.explanation: When it is dark and hard to see, increase the distance between you and other vehicles. Use your headlights properly, following rules for high and low beams. Do not look directly at oncoming headlights as the bright light can blind you.

questions.question: A car suddenly cuts in front of you. What should you do first?

options.text: Honk your horn and brake hard.
Release the gas pedal.
Swerve into the next lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release the gas pedal.
questions.explanation: If a vehicle cuts in front of you too closely, release the gas pedal. This creates more space between you and the other vehicle without forcing you to brake hard or swerve.

questions.question: When can you legally block an intersection?

options.text: If you entered on a green light.
During rush hour traffic.
Never.

questions.correctAnswerText: Never.
questions.explanation: Do not enter an intersection unless you can cross it completely before the light turns red. If you block the intersection, you can get a ticket.

questions.question: A yellow light means the red light is coming. If you are already in the intersection when the light turns yellow, what should you do?

options.text: Stop.
Keep going and safely clear the intersection.
Speed up to avoid an accident.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep going and safely clear the intersection.
questions.explanation: If you are already in the intersection when the light turns yellow, keep moving to clear it as quickly and safely as possible.

questions.question: A car ahead has high beams on and it is hard for you to see. What should you do?

options.text: Look toward the left edge of your lane.
Look toward the right edge of your lane.
Look straight ahead in your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look toward the right edge of your lane.
questions.explanation: Do not look directly at the bright headlights. Instead, look toward the right edge of your lane and watch the other car from the corner of your eye.

questions.question: Why should you look far ahead when driving on the highway?

options.text: It helps you keep up with traffic.
It reduces sudden braking or lane changes.
It helps you spot police officers.

questions.correctAnswerText: It reduces sudden braking or lane changes.
questions.explanation: Looking ahead helps you avoid sudden braking or turning. You can be ready to stop or change lanes safely. This makes driving safer, saves fuel, and helps traffic move smoothly.

questions.question: What should you do if there is a deep puddle on the road?

options.text: Keep your speed the same to get through the water.
Avoid the puddle if you can.
Put the car in neutral as you drive through.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid the puddle if you can.
questions.explanation: Avoid slippery areas like puddles, ice, wet leaves, and oil. Dry, solid surfaces are the safest for driving.
